summary: Stream offset skew after intermediary HTTP/2 server-push via reverse proxy causes partial-choice duplication
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports repeated partial tokens and duplicated early fragments when resuming SSE streams after a short disconnect. The pattern is consistent when requests route through their managed reverse proxy that enables HTTP/2 server-push (Apache/mod_http2).

Impact:
- Customer-facing chat UI shows duplicated early phrases and missing later tokens for ~10% of resumed streams.
- Users report 15% of resumed messages requiring manual refresh, affecting perceived reliability for the enterprise customer (billing tier: enterprise).

Environment:
- Customer runs web client in browser behind corporate reverse proxy (Apache 2.4 + mod_http2) + internal CDN.
- Redwood API requests route through our api-gateway -> edge-proxy -> serving-runtime in us-east.
- Model: redwood/gpt-3.5-small pinned.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Open web chat session (long-running conversation, ~1k token context).
2) Trigger generation with streaming SSE response (streaming=true).
3) Simulate short network blip (~2s) that closes client TCP connection; client attempts immediate reconnect.
4) Observe resumed stream: initial fragments duplicated, later fragments missing or reordered.

Minimal repro (curl):
- Customer captured reproduction using http2-capable curl + netcat to simulate proxy push. Example (approx):
  curl --http2 -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?stream=true&model=redwood/gpt-3.5-small" 2>&1 | sed -n '1,200p'

Observed logs (customer):
- Edge logs show connection reset followed by two requests within 500ms reusing the same session affinity token.
- Proxy logs include: "H2-PUSH: stream 15 associated with stream 3" and several 200 OK but with "content-length: chunked" re-chunking.

Additional context:
- This customer only sees the problem when their proxy has H2 server-push enabled. They attempted disabling push and reported the symptom disappears.
- Others on standard load-balanced paths have not reproduced; however, we have similar-but-different tickets referencing fragmented chunks and proxy reordering (linked issues above).
comments: 2026-03-10 | Aisha Tan (Support): Customer opened case with chat transcript and edge/log snippets. Customer asserts issue began after proxy upgrade to mod_http2 1.15.
2026-03-10 | Marco Ruiz (SRE): Assigned for investigation. Requested packet capture and exact proxy config. Asked customer for TLS termination details and whether connection pooling was in use.

2026-03-11 | NeoDoc (Customer): Provided proxy config excerpt: 'H2Push on; H2PushPriorityPolicy interleave; SetEnv proxy-sendchunks on'. Also attached pcap showing server-push frames interleaved with reset. Customer confirms disabling H2Push removes the duplication.

2026-03-11 | Marco Ruiz (SRE): Reproduced locally using a test proxy with server-push enabled. Observed that our SSE framing boundary ("data: {json}\n\n") can be split across HTTP/2 DATA frames that are then associated with server-push streams; reassembly at the edge-proxy layer produced an off-by-one offset in event boundaries during rapid reconnects.

2026-03-12 | Eng (Serving Runtime): Noted possible root cause: when connection is reset and a subsequent request reuses the same HTTP/2 session, the proxy may deliver leftover pushed DATA frames tied to previous stream IDs before the new stream's end-event. This causes the client to see duplicated early fragments and missing terminal fragments because metadata end markers are misassociated.

2026-03-13 | Marco Ruiz (SRE): Proposed mitigation to treat server-push frames as ephemeral for SSE endpoints and drop any pushed frames that are not explicitly associated with an active stream ID in the runtime's reassembly logic. Filed internal follow-up INT-3420 to add stricter stream-id validation at the api-gateway layer.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Proxy-level re-chunking + HTTP/2 server-push can shuffle DATA frames across stream boundaries during quick reconnects, producing event boundary misalignment in our SSE reassembler.

Hypothesis 2: Client reconnect semantics + reused session affinity token allow race where pushed fragments from prior stream arrive and are stitched into the resumed stream before the resumed stream's final end-event is observed.
Reproducer created: Local apache/mux proxy with H2Push on + curl --http2 -N. Able to produce partial-choice duplication in ~30% of trials when adding a forced connection reset between frames.

Edge observations: api-gateway currently relies on sequential assembly by stream connection and does not validate HTTP/2 PUSH_PROMISE lineage robustly for SSE endpoints. Flow currently treats DATA frames arriving on the session as belonging to the most recently active stream if stream ids overlap due to proxy mapping.
resolution:
Workaround (customer): Disable HTTP/2 server-push on their reverse proxy (confirmed fix).

Short-term server-side mitigation: Implemented gating in api-gateway to reject or ignore HTTP/2 pushed DATA frames for SSE/streaming endpoints, and added conservative stream-id validation (edge patch deployed to us-east as a config toggle). Rolled out to 10% of edge hosts 2026-03-13 04:20UTC.

Long-term fix: Engineering to add deterministic stream lineage checks and stricter framing reassembly at api-gateway + update docs recommending disabling H2 server-push for streaming endpoints. Tracked in INT-3420 (add stream-id lineage validation) and ENG-5042 (update docs + SDK guidance).

Follow-ups: Monitor customer telemetry for 48 hours; pending customer confirmation (requested 2026-03-13). If telemetry remains clean, close ticket and document as KB article 'Proxy server-push interactions with SSE streaming'.
